summary:
The patient sustained a motor vehicle accident in September 2023 resulting in left arm fractures, specifically involving the humerus and radius. Emergency orthopedic surgery was performed with open reduction and internal fixation. The patient also presented with cervicalgia following the injury.

The patient had prior neck pain and imaging findings from a gym weightlifting accident in 2022, including mild degenerative disc disease and a posterior disc bulge at C5-C6. Records indicate this disc bulge may have been a pre-existing condition.

Following surgery, the patient underwent an extensive course of rehabilitation including over sixty physical therapy sessions across two facilities over a period of several months. Treatment addressed both the left arm fractures and persistent cervical symptoms, which were frequently provoked during therapy. Pain management included both narcotic and non-narcotic medications as well as muscle relaxants.

By discharge from physical therapy, the patient had achieved substantial functional improvements with well-healed fractures and stable internal hardware. However, significant deficits remain. The patient demonstrates persistent restriction in left elbow range of motion, decreased grip strength, and chronic cervical pain with stiffness. Ongoing limitations in forearm and shoulder mobility have persisted despite intensive rehabilitation.
